turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt_extrapolation_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns
    process/composition columns (Sb, O, Te, Co, Mg, Sn, Se, Pb, Si, S, Cu,
    Ge, Ni, Bi, Ti, Fe, Zn, In, Zr, Ca, Ag, T) and `target` (the measured zT
    measured at each row's own temperature T (K)).
  - b3_te_zt_extrapolation_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT at 800 K
    was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same
    process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT at 800
K, then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I treated composition as the main similarity driver and used T mainly as a scaling/extrapolation variable, since zT generally rises from 300–500 K toward 800 K. I down-weighted the lone Sb–Co–Ti point with zT ≈ 21.63 as an anomalous outlier rather than letting it dominate nearest-neighbor extrapolation.

The strongest 800 K candidates are those matching/near the best high-T training families:
- Pb–Te/Sb compositions are the clearest top performers: c043 and c046 closely match training rows with zT ≈ 1.13 and ≈ 0.96 at 500 K.
- Sb–Co/skutterudite-like compositions show strong T dependence and high 500 K values, favoring c061 and c012.
- Mg–Si high-temperature compositions are also favorable, with c090 matching a strong training composition.

Final: c043, c046, c061, c012, c090
